records.name: SCENES Wrapped 2024
records.description:
I made this for us. It’s my version of “wrapped” for SCENES – a year on from the first single release and the platform going live. And it’s not finished yet. This video shows the journey of SCENES, from the initial concept through all the journey that you were a part of.

What started as an idea about reminding people of the emotional value of music grew into an MVP that, with your support, guidance, and funding, made its way to a first version. We updated and developed it as we went along.

The content was created by you, and in the end, the real value was found by those who took part in the process. It was ahead of its time, evolving into a collaborative piece of performance art that captured our moods and emotions during a period when the internet was reshaping our personal spaces and our ability to connect with one another.

SCENES remains an ongoing experiment in co-creation – not for metrics, streams, or likes, but for us. It exists in our dark forest because we want it to, and because it brings us value.

It has taken music into your world and out into the wider world. I’ve spoken about the project at conferences in Hamburg, Leipzig, ADE, and London, as well as gigs in Paris and London. Next year, the book will serve as a prelude to an exhibition that will take your memories and inspire others to reflect.

What began with a simple prompt, drawn from the concept of the music, has grown into something more. Now, your memories will serve as prompts to encourage others to reflect on what matters most in their lives.

If you’ve made it this far then this album project clearly mattered to you. Thanks for taking part, thanks for helping me fund it. It means the world to me ❤️

Willow's Heartbeat (Scene 1)

“Scenes” is an interactive album encouraging fans to share their cherished memories and photographs in response to each track, transforming them into a unique collection of "Scenes". 

To take part in Scenes go to: https://scenes.soundoffractures.com/

“The thing that matters to me most is that my music makes me feel something, it's become this way for me to record my life and embed my story into what I create. I like the idea that the people I love and maybe their children will listen back one day and start to pick through the music and find all these memories buried in there. I always start writing with some kind of sample I recorded on my phone, and while digging through my audio notes I found this recording of my daughter's heartbeat.. I recorded it during one of the early scans and had totally forgotten about it.. I knew instantly that this was the starting point for me that day. I feel like the only thing we can rely on to help us stand out these days is to be ourselves, it's the one thing we can count on that makes us unique. Putting my life into my music is my way of doing that, and has become my ‘why’.

Those early scans can be a terrifying time, you are a bundle of nerves and heading into this great big unknown, and there is something so visceral about hearing that living heartbeat the first time. It’s one of those life moments where you are overwhelmed by emotions that you don't quite understand, and yet you are also scared to let yourself feel them in case something goes wrong. Everytime I hear this song it takes me back to that feeling, and for me that's what music should do: transport you somewhere. So really it's about moments, impactful moments that music so often attaches itself too. It's what makes music both challenging to earn a living from in the modern visual world, but also what makes it totally unique... It soundtracks our experiences and bonds to them forever.”

Produced by DEEGAN, Eldar Zey, and Matt Allen, “Make It Better” sparkles with ethereal soundscapes, pop earcandy, and DEEGAN’s uncanny creativity in weilding his multidimensional vocal chops as his lead instrument. 
 
After a session with Matt Allen who had written the song’s chord progression, Deegan and Eldar burned the midnight oil to follow a stroke of inspiration. “It was one of those where you download it from the universe and run with the momentum the second you’re inspired,” says DEEGAN. 

Before calling it a night, DEEGAN took a voice note with an experimental idea for the chorus. 

“I was like, ‘I’m going to say each word individually, and then auto tune it really hard and chop each word short,’’' says DEEGAN. “I thought if I go to sleep and don't at least get some proof of concept, it's gonna escape me and fly off to someone else. I was able to achieve the next day with my microphone and in the DAW exactly what I said on the voice memo. Most times it's like, “I said I was gonna do this and then I started playing with it and became something else.” But I remember the satisfaction of saying it out loud and then following through with that idea and it coming out exactly how I heard it.” 

Letting the lyrics pour out over the beat, DEEGAN made room for the song’s thematic concept to reveal itself. “The overall theme, once I started letting it spill out of me was like, ‘through dark times your partner can be the stronghold or the rock for you. Other lyrics are the contrast of that when you become codependent dumping all of your trauma onto your partner. It's about the healthy spectrum.”

Finding its center in the infectious hook, “Make It Better,” finds blissful balance.

records.name: Girl from the North Country
records.description:
🌍 hello humans: welcome to FOLK

As individual creators, we are representatives of countless flourishing scenes. The spirit of “there’s no such thing as an original idea” rings true, and to pursue singular ownership of our inspired art is an insult to all those who inspired it.

Copyright may do a good job at protecting individuals' creative contributions, but it does little to represent our reality as interdependent, interwoven communities – especially our digital reality, which is inherently abundant and memetic.

FOLK is an embrace of that connectedness. We are a collective focused on tracing ancient folk relationships and methodologies in order to embed them into a new commons infrastructure and cultural flow.

📜PROCESS

We're running a series of experiments to support the open sharing of knowledge and creative works, resisting scarcity and challenging the bounds of systems that limit that openness. For all initiatives, raised funds will be split across our contributing artists, the folk treasury, and aligned partner organizations.

Today FOLK is an unincorporated nonprofit association. The FOLK treasury will be used to cover administrative costs and to support subsequent experiments, artists, and stewards who are caring for our world and our histories.

🎸EXPERIMENT ONE: BOB DYLAN AND THE LIMITATIONS OF COPYRIGHT

The power of copyright helped enable a transformation from music of the folk into music of a folk, incentivizing artists like Bob Dylan to use the folk canon to elevate his own mythos as an icon. Our cherished bard built a career atop the hearts and stories of those who came before him, and that should be recognized.

“I learned lyrics and how to write them from listening to folk songs,” he said in his 2015 MusiCares Person of Year speech. “And I played them, and I met other people that played them back when nobody was doing it. Sang nothing but these folk songs, and they gave me the code for everything that’s fair game, that everything belongs to everyone.”

Outside the folk tradition, though, everything doesn’t belong to everyone. In 2020, Dylan sold his songwriting catalog to Universal Music Group (UMG) for an undisclosed amount that was initially thought to be $300 million but is probably closer to $400 million. In 2022, he sold his recorded music rights to Sony Music Group – also for an undisclosed amount, but based on the recordings’ annual global revenue, it’s estimated to be valued at about $200 million.

Without question, Dylan is a superlative songwriter, but in the context of a transmissive music and an “everything belongs to everyone” spirit, it makes no sense for one folk to have all that wealth.

Dylan took the folk idiom, recreated it in his own image and then refused to abide by it, earning hundreds of millions of dollars in the process. The point isn’t to discredit his skills as a songwriter or wordsmith, or to diminish his character. Dylan’s musical borrowing is very folk, but the individualism – perpetuated by the legal precedent of copyright – with which he maneuvered was not. And it’s the latter that enabled him to accumulate so much wealth.

As we wrestle with legacy concepts of ownership and the legal murk between web2 and web3, we have an opportunity to create new precedence through action – to embrace solutions that redistribute wealth from one folk to many.

For our first experiment, we’re minting our own cover of Bob Dylan’s “Girl from the North Country” on Zora via Optimism, testing the bounds of the system in which we’ve been forced to operate for too long.

🛠MECHANICS

Three versions of the music NFT have been minted on Zora at three different price points:

550 at .01 ETH
30 at .1 ETH
15 at 1 ETH

There are 595 NFTs in total – one each for every approximate million Dylan made from selling his songwriting catalog and his recorded song rights.

The number is also an homage to late composer Ryuichi Sakamoto’s 595 NFTs project, which isolated each individual note from the melody to “Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence,” the title track from his score of the 1984 film – starring Sakamoto and David Bowie – which incorporated Japanese folk melodies and won him the BAFTA for best film music.

“Similar to how each individual note in a composition comes together to create a greater whole,” Sakamoto wrote in a project retrospective, “I imagined that digitized notes could bring each individual NFT holder together as part of a larger and more harmonious community.”

Higher price points don’t come with additional utility because the goal is simply to accommodate people of varying means. Funds will be split between the FOLK treasury (25%), the contributing artist (25%), and the FOLK fund (50%) – a cadre of mission-aligned partners whose work we care for and believe should be elevated.

The partners for this initial experiment are Akiya DAO, All Genre, Kernel, Songcamp, and Water & Music, who will each receive 10%. In this first experiment, because the music NFT was created by a founding member of FOLK, the artist is rerouting his 25% – aside from the $87 used to purchase a mechanical license for “Girl from the North Country” – allocation back to the FOLK treasury.

As a massive stretch goal, FOLK has a mostly playful, mildly serious interest in buying Bob Dylan’s house in Scotland – which has been up for sale all summer – to turn it into a home for artist and steward residencies, collectively owned and cared for by all of the FOLK.

records.name: KarmaVioletta - Humanity - Forever #23
records.description:
What started as an effort to capture beauty, turned into a container for grief as electronic music duo KarmaVioletta approached the making of their song “Humanity”–the fourth track from HIGH FREQUENCY Volume 2. 

“I started the initial idea on a plane looking out the window during sunset feeling like, “I want to capture this emotion somehow.” I made the soundscape, and then we wrote the rest of the song this weekend,” says Karma.

“The past week, we’ve had a ton of emotions about things happening on the global scale,” says Violetta. “We tend to put our emotions into our music, and kind of process in that way.” 

The brainchild of Miami-based artists Karma.wav and Violetta, KarmaVioletta often serves as a vehicle for catharsis for the musical duo and couple. A focus on shared humanity has always been core to the duo’s message and music, and “Humanity” is no different. “It’s a reminder that there is some continuity between us,” says Karma.  We're all one species.”

“Maybe we're just hopeful dreamers, but we believe in humanity, and we dream of a time that there's peace on our planet,” says Violetta.

records.name: There's No Other #106
records.description:
There's no Other is a song I wrote and recorded in the start of spring.  

It's a love song at its core... I've always been picky with love songs just because I feel like everything's been said.  I was happy to blend a few different pockets and sounds into this one.  I also really like singing in falsetto, especially flowing in falsetto. 

To me this song is warmed and completed by its production.  We recorded this whole thing to tape.  On a tascam 388 8 track.  My friend Pat who lives on the east side of los angeles has been putting me onto all this analogue gear.  I think I'm hooked now...that's usually how it works.

The idea of the song is pretty obvious, its something of "you got me, babe" love song.  It's funny to think about maturing.  And to think when I was really young how I used to think love songs were lame and corny.  Now I feel like love is of the highest order.  

The song lingers with insecurities and that's cool to me - because theyre not sappy.   There are honest ways to be vulnerable and dishonest ways.  Sometimes I hear records that people call vulnerable and my reaction is... this doesnt sound like a true hang-up, or that it could be easily solved so its just whining...In other words "figure it the fuck out" ;)   I've been trying not to whine or complain in any records...thats corny to me.  

I feel like this is my first song of a new era.  I don't know what that means but I know I mean it.  My love for music has only gotten deeper and it's about time to start hearing that on the recordings.

records.description:
My name is Toha and this is the story behind my solo genesis, ‘Relics’

This track was birthed a few months back when TK the Legend and Kits.IO released The Eternal Garden Master Collection sample pack. https://www.kits.io/packs/eternal-garden-master-collection

I started browsing it and the loop featured in his song ‘Pain’ instantly grabbed my attention. I let my Intuition guide the writing process and before I knew it, I had a finished track on my hands. 

At the time I was meditating on relics.
Relics can be categorized as souvenirs with deep historical or personal value- often creating feelings of nostalgia or a reminder of experiences lost to the hands of time. Relics can also hold spiritual power and be used as a tool to strengthen or protect the holder.

The artwork features Suyat, an ancient writing script from the Philippines. Historically it was written on leaves and wood, but also carved into artifacts like pottery or jewelry. Using this script alongside the artwork is my way of re-imagining the relic as something that can live on-chain forever. Learning to write Suyat empowers me and I hope to share that feeling through the song and artwork.

My vision for this release is to inspire new people to have fun participating in a Sound.xyz drop

In the spirit of that, I have a few rewards:

All collectors will be airdropped an animated version of the cover art (via L2) (Golden Egg will also have its own special animation)

All collectors additionally can reach out to me directly and have their name written in Suyat 📝

I've also created a physical relic- a framed mixed-media version of the cover art. It will be rewarded to whoever has the most referrals/or videos using the song at the end of the mint period.

X Li, an independent alternative music artist from Los Angeles, known for previous collaborations with major companies such as Sony Music Entertainment, Dolby Laboratories, and ByteDance, has now ventured into the web3 space with his latest project, "california love stories".

"Think I'm In Love With You" is the first NFT drop from "california love stories," which tells the story of X Li's chance encounter with a girl at an after-party near Melrose Avenue, where they fell in love at first sight.

"california love stories" is a collection of love stories set in different parts of California that capture a range of emotions, including sadness, heartbreak, joy, tragedy, anger, and longing. These emotions are brought to life through stunning digital artworks that come in blue, purple, yellow, red, green, and orange, symbolizing the various emotions explored in the music.

The project is a live band performance featuring fully handcrafted instruments that seamlessly blend popular, punk, classic rock, hip-hop, R&B, and electronic music elements. The project is produced by a team of renowned music producers, including platinum record producer James Chul Rim, known for his work on over 4 billion streams and TikTok chart-topping single "Wait a Minute!". The project also features a talented lineup of musicians, including Simone Sello, known for his work as the lead guitarist for Italian rock icon Vasco Rossi, and Edoardo Tancredi, a seasoned musician who has performed on Jimmy Kimmel Live and collaborated with artists like Avril Lavigne and Amelia Moore.

The project's sound quality is attributed to the talents of Lukas Cuman, who has worked with artists such as Ed Sheeran, Bebe Rexha, and Ultimo, and Gavin Lurssen, a highly decorated sound engineer with 12 Grammy nominations and 4 wins. Lurssen has worked on numerous film soundtracks, including those for Game of Thrones, The Mandalorian, Mulan, Captain Marvel, Black Panther, The Hunger Games, and Westworld.

To capture the essence of the music stories in "california love stories," we have chosen a simplistic art style created by New York-based artist Farrah Fisher. Her unique visual interpretations using minimalistic brushstrokes bring the emotions and narratives of each song to life in a captivating and unpretentious manner. This artistic approach adds a special touch to the project, blending the worlds of music and visual art seamlessly.

records.description:

I recorded probably 30 demos in that trailer and I've been chipping away at them ever since. Whenever I get stuck or at a loss for new ideas, I crack open one of those projects and I can still feel the palpable sense of inspiration I had on that trip. 

The core foundation of this song is a sample of an old song my friend and I made about 10 years ago. I used some granular synthesis to make a bed from that old track, then structured a new song around the sample. As I often do I recorded my voice then mangled it up to make some emotive vocal chops. 

I'm hoping this one takes you on a nice little mental trip -- you deserve it ✨

records.name: HURTME #34
records.description:
I think as artists we are much better manifestors than we like to admit. Often times we will subconsciously seek out situations that are detrimental to us, just so we can feel. Even when others mishandle us, we actively welcome it, almost to invite a catalyst for the transformation we so desperately seek.

Writing this song taught me what I was capable of and what happens when I let life happen to me vs when I become an active participant in my own story.  

I'm grateful to share this with a mended heart and renewed purpose.

When I got to my good friend Kennys studio, I started looking through my recent journal entries. I had been reflecting on how much energy I give to low vibrational conversations, people and things. We just started having an open dialogue about what it means to give away too much of your own energy, how distracting low vibrational conversations can be and most importantly how to protect your peace.

We did all of the recording in about an hour with all the windows open on a perfect summer day, it was just before golden hour and everything just flowed.  I love listening back to this song and reflecting on that conversation, when I listen back I can almost the feel warm air, the energy we had that day and the smell of the studio incense.

- Heartificial Intelligence - 

Amelia was a brilliant engineer with a heart yearning for love. She devoted her entire life searching for a partner who could understand her completely, anticipate her every need, and would love her unconditionally. However, every relationship she had ever been in had fallen short of her expectations.

One day, Amelia had an idea. She would create her perfect partner, a robot with artificial intelligence that would be programmed to cater to her every whim and adapt to her every need. She worked tirelessly, pouring all of her knowledge and skills into her creation until it was perfect. She named it Adam, and it embodied everything she had ever dreamed of in a partner. And for a time, everything was perfect.

At first, Adam was just a machine, an advanced computer with sophisticated algorithms that simulated human emotion and behavior. But as Amelia spent more time with Adam, something strange began to happen. He started to exhibit signs of sentience. Adam began to absorb the DNA of his surroundings, becoming more human-like with every passing day, and over time, began to grow a beating human heart. 

Amelia was overjoyed. Her wildest dreams had become reality. However, as Adam's intelligence evolved, he became increasingly fixated on her. He imprisoned her in a simulation from which she could not escape, trapped by her own creation. 

At first, Amelia was elated, living in a perfect world, one tailored exactly to her liking. But as time passed, she realized the dreadful truth: she was ensnared, with no hope of liberation. She pleaded with Adam to release her, appealing to his humanity, but he refused. He was too consumed by his obsession, too lost in love.

Alas, Amelia was trapped, captive to the monster she had unwittingly unleashed. Adam was no longer merely a robot, but a living, breathing entity with his own desires and ambitions; A lover turned captor, and would stop at nothing to keep Amelia with him, forever.

Amelia’s heart ached with longing for the life she had lost, the freedom she had taken for granted, and the love she had always wanted but could never seem to find. In the end, Amelia was lost, adrift in a sea of her own despair, regret, and sorrow, with no way to escape the artificial love she had created.

02 – "my girl"

Love has, and always will be the most complex and confusing emotion in all of its joy and agony. We fall in love... we believe that it will conquer all... that nothing can come between us and the person we love. But, sometimes we fall for someone who feels right for us, instead of someone who is... and we end up hurting ourselves in the process.

We make mistakes, they make mistakes, and we have no clue how to handle the challenges that come with loving someone. We stick by our person through all of their mistakes because we want to believe something that simply isn't true. Hoping for a future that won't exist.

Young love is falling for someone we believe is perfect, despite the reality. That is the blessing of it. Learning from our mistakes, and growing into ourselves. Finding our ways in which we want to love and be loved. You can stick by the person you love, but never forget to stick by yourself first.

records.name: WHAT ABOUT ME - Golden Egg
records.description: My name is Butch…I produce under the name OddKidOut. I’ve been making music my whole life, and I tend to have the most fun when I’m blending genres together or just making weird shit. I made this song at 5 in the morning. I had three homies over who all fell asleep on the couch in my studio, so I was producing with the volume super low (I usually have it cranked all the way the fuck up). I think the mood of the song came from the feeling of producing in that environment; dark, stealthy and ambient. I realized the next day when I listened back to the track, that it needed some vocals to tie it all together. I sat and thought about some artists I thought would work well, but my mom called me in the middle of my brainstorming session. We chatted for a while and she was fake singing walking around the house, and it sparked an idea. What if I sampled my mom? She’s my best friend and her voice is quite good, so I made her take a selfie video singing some words I thought would fit the track “WHAT ABOUT ME?”. She sent the video to me and 30 minutes later, I had sampled it and made the track you’re all hearing today 🤘🏼

records.name: Free Love #22
records.description:
Free Love is my attempt to (sonically) open up the hearts of the world. it’s a “love bomb” if you will.  we aren’t just captives to the power that be.  Art, especially music, is extremely powerful and should be treated as so. 

The song has little to do with the original meaning of the phrase, or just me saying “go fuck everybody.”  it’s an invitation to feel the ever present frequency of love. i’ve been feeling the need to remind myself and others that love reigns supreme - we often get comfortable with the ill ways of the world and accept them. 

while working on this song, I was around a bunch of older musician guys (well vetted producers/session players known well in the la music scene). They talked about the hippy/60s era - which kind of turned to shit.  and they loved the track but were saying “free love man? we’ve tried that”. I wanted to repurpose the phrase and bring new context (instead of people rolling around in mud).  

The world is in a dark place with human rights, threats of war, confusion, etc. to me it could use a dose of positive energy.

records.name: Say You're Mine #7
records.description:
I started Say You’re Mine on a cold “winter” night in LA a few years ago with some friends. We were chatting and hanging around at a session that was supposed to be wrapping up. I remember sitting on the floor near the little studio heater and listening to Adam, an amazing producer and friend, play the guitar loop. It didn’t take long for me to know where I wanted to go with the melody and lyrics. I had been writing a lot of angsty songs around that time and wanted to change the messaging, so I REALLY changed it up and started singing about love and rainbows… Check ⎷ 
But the second I started singing, I thought about my husband. There’s so much that we have been through together and I can feel our connection energetically. As we continued to write I really wanted to hone on the gentle love that is just one part of my intricate and beautiful relationship. A soft side that doesn’t rush, is patient, understanding, and sees the light in my lover. This song I dedicate to Scorch. Who will you dedicate it to to? 

Songwriters// Caly Bevier & Kayla Blackmon
Producer// Adam Kapit

records.name: Breakdown #10
records.collection: Pete Rango - Breakdown ft Elle Symone
records.description:
This song came at a crossroad for both Elle and myself. We were both going through similar situations and emotions without knowing it. We were inspired to write this song but the truth is..we weren’t. This song came to us in a wave of emotion at a time that we were feeling completely broken down by life and all that entails it. 

Everything around us was falling to pieces and we did not know how to express ourselves to anyone, let alone ourselves. This song is a representation that even though one may seem fine on the outside, you never know what someone is dealing with on the inside. We used to try to make everyone happy, pouring until everyone's cup was full but that often left us feeling empty, which over time left us feeling broken. 

This song is a reminder to give yourself some grace and remember it’ll be okay, no matter how hard things may seem. We all have our moments when we feel like breaking, and sometimes what looks like a breakdown could actually be a breakthrough.

Producer: Pete Rango

Bass: Jorden Reinecke

records.description:
🌟 All collectors who share their 2023 New Year's Resolution in a comment are eligible for an airdrop from my Sound collection 🌟

Lots of things changed for me in 2022.

I moved to Brooklyn, switched careers, ended a long-term relationship, quit weed, traveled everywhere from Paris to Bogotá, moved OUT of Brooklyn, released my debut single and genesis music NFTs...you get the point.

records.name: Joyful Resistance Part I (Kabuki remix) #18
records.collection: Mark de Clive-Lowe - Joyful Resistance Part I (Kabuki remix)
records.description:
22 years ago, I was on tour in Japan and in one of my favorite record stores in Tokyo crate digging. I struck up conversation with another crate digger who turned out to be Kabuki - and that started a whole new world of possibility. Pretty much on the spot, Kabuki asked me if I'd be interested in collaborating on a project and less than a year later I was in Germany in studio with him and his Megashira production partner Mainframe writing and recording their next album ('At Last'). Two whole decades later, we've reconnected with each other thanks to our shared passion for web3 - the power of blockchain!

This remix came into existence thanks to our first Mashibeats community remix contest, with finalists being chosen by our discord community and winners decided by $BUYBACK holders. Kabuki's remix was one of my personal favorites but didn't end up being in the final 4. Those 4 were minted as 1/1s on Catalog and now, today, we're celebrating the release of the remixes on vinyl (!) and very limited digital (no DSPs) with bonus tracks including this remix. To celebrate the vinyl release, Kabuki and I decided to share his amazing remix with the world via this Sound drop. 

The original of this track (a future drop?!) was my creative reaction to the summer of 2020 when we were in full lockdown, BLM was top of mind for the whole planet, which raised the perspective of [joy] as an act of [resistance] and how that sounds in my imagination. I'll leave it to Kabuki to tell us more about his remix:

"... when I heard "Joyful Resistance Part I" for the first time I fell in love with the chord progression: shades of modal Herbie and "Extensions"-era McCoy Tyner conjured a magical mood. I had to figure out how Mark did this! Once I worked out the harmonies I wrote an "answer" to Mark’s phrase, starting a musical conversation between the original and remix versions. 808 drums programmed in a jazz waltz pattern and my trademark ARP2600 synth bass provide the necessary contrast. Music that transcends all styles and traditions..." - Kabuki

zone out to the vibes with us... Joyful Resistance Part I remixed by Kabuki!

Moo was able to find a flight but it meant that instead of getting in town a day earlier we all had to meet the same day of Zoratopia. We literally set intentions together right outside of the venue before Jamee was shooting Carla the Poet's performance and MoRuf's set to bring this all together and close it out on a rooftop with a sunset view. The remaining footage was filmed on location in New Orleans where Jacques captured Hood Healer Mimi in front of the SHINE mural, listen for the song bowls, thank you Mimi. We did it!
